recall.define: Define symptom, first divergence, minimal reproducer, invariant, bisection and core dump without the glossary and name the reading that defines each.
recall.distinguish: Give the distinction and an example for: symptom versus cause; breakpoint versus watchpoint; abnormal termination versus HardFault; optimized-out versus uninitialized; deterministic replay versus repeated stress run.
recall.apply: A service terminates abnormally with SIGSEGV once per day. Using symptom, competing hypothesis, discriminating test, minimal reproducer and regression test, lay out the diagnosis sequence, say which observation would separate a use-after-free from an out-of-bounds write, and which term names the evidence a sanitizer run adds.

entries.definition: The observable deviation from the contract (a wrong output, a signal, a hang, a timing miss) that starts a diagnosis; it is evidence about the failure's effect, not its cause, and the same symptom can arise from many causes.
entries.misconception: The line where the program stopped is where the bug is.

entries.definition: A supported mechanism or violated precondition/invariant explaining a failure under stated conditions. Establish it through a relevant execution history, competing explanations and discriminating evidence. The earliest observed invalid transition may narrow the cause without proving it is the unique or earliest causal event in an unobserved history.
entries.misconception: Making the symptom disappear proves the cause was found.

entries.definition: The earliest supported mismatch between an observed state and a justified reference contract or prediction at the available observation points. Instrumentation gaps can hide an earlier mismatch; an incorrect prediction can create an apparent divergence. Locating it narrows investigation but does not by itself prove the complete cause.
idiom: find the first divergence before editing anything
entries.misconception: Debugging starts at the failure and works forward.

entries.definition: An alternative explanation of the symptom that fits the same evidence; a discriminating test is an observation or experiment whose outcome differs under the two hypotheses, and diagnosis proceeds by eliminating hypotheses, not by confirming the favorite.

The smallest input, configuration and program fragment that still produces the symptom, obtained by systematic reduction (delta debugging); it is the artifact that makes a defect reportable, bisectable and testable.

authority.locator: Section 4 A Minimizing Algorithm — Figure 1 and reduction rules (PDF pp.3–4)

entries.misconception: A reproducer must be a whole program.

entries.definition: A property of program state that must hold at specified points (between operations on a data structure, at loop heads); checking invariants converts a vague symptom into the first operation that broke one, and repairing the invariant, not the symptom, is the fix.
idiom: assert the ring invariant after every push and pop

entries.definition: Binary search over an ordered set of candidates (commits, inputs, build flags, code regions) for the first one that exhibits the symptom; git bisect automates it over history, and the same idea reduces inputs and configurations.

authority.locator: Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3)

entries.misconception: Bisection finds the cause (it finds the first bad candidate, which must still be diagnosed).

entries.definition: A recorded process image usable with matching executable/debug information to examine captured registers and memory. It may be produced on signal termination or captured from a running process; selected mappings can be omitted. Permissions, limits and collection policy affect availability. A captured state is evidence at a point in an execution, not a complete causal history.
entries.misconception: A core dump shows what the program did (it shows only the final state).

entries.definition: A debugger-inserted stop at a code address (software breakpoint, by patching an instruction) or on an address match in a hardware comparator; stopping changes timing, which matters for interrupt-driven and concurrent code.

authority.locator: 5.1.1 Setting Breakpoints — break locspec and multiple locations

distinguish_from.distinction: A watchpoint stops on a data access rather than on reaching an instruction; hardware watchpoints are scarce and their width is limited.

entries.misconception: Breakpoints are free of side effects.

entries.definition: A stop triggered by a read or write of a memory location, implemented by hardware comparators (DWT on Cortex-M, debug registers on x86) or, far more slowly, by single-stepping; the tool for finding who corrupts a variable.

authority.locator: 5.1.2 Setting Watchpoints — hardware/software limits and watched-object scope
C1.8.1 The DWT comparators — opening overview and watchpoint timing (C1-719, C1-730)

entries.misconception: A watchpoint on a struct watches every member (hardware watchpoints have a maximum width).

entries.definition: A variable or frame the debugger cannot show because optimization eliminated or relocated it; the program is correct, the debug information is incomplete. It is distinct from an uninitialized or corrupted value and is the usual reason to debug at -Og or read the disassembly.

authority.locator: 10.3 Program Variables — selected-frame scope and incomplete or optimized state

entries.definition: Interpret captured Cortex-M fault status, valid address registers and a trustworthy exception frame under the exact architecture. Check MMARVALID/BFARVALID, escalation and stacking/unstacking errors before attributing an address or PC. Imprecise faults and damaged frames may not identify the original instruction. Status bits accumulate and are write-one-to-clear, so preserve evidence before clearing it.

authority.locator: B3.2.14–B3.2.18, pp.B3-609–614: CFSR, BFSR, HFSR, MMFAR and BFAR

entries.misconception: A HardFault handler that blinks an LED is diagnosis.

entries.definition: The chain of stack frames from the current function to the entry point, reconstructed from frame pointers or unwind tables; a corrupted stack or omitted frame pointers produce a misleading backtrace, which is itself a symptom.

authority.locator: 8.2 Backtraces — selected-thread frames, bt full and optimized-out arguments

entries.definition: Re-executing a failure with recorded inputs, schedules and timing so that it recurs on demand; a replay establishes causality where a repeated stress run only establishes frequency.

authority.locator: Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3)

distinguish_from.distinction: A stress run shows that a failure occurs under load; it is neither a reproducer nor a proof of its absence.

entries.misconception: Running the test a thousand times is a diagnosis.

entries.definition: The minimal reproducer turned into a permanent automated check that fails if the defect returns; the last step of every diagnosis, and the evidence that the repair addressed the cause rather than the symptom.
entries.misconception: A fix is complete when the symptom is gone.

entries.definition: Compiler instrumentation (AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, ThreadSanitizer) that checks memory accesses, undefined operations or data races at run time and reports the first violation with a stack trace; it observes only executed paths and changes layout and timing.

authority.locator: 5.2 Continuing and Stepping — continue, step, next, finish, until, stepi and nexti

entries.misconception: A clean sanitizer run proves the absence of undefined behavior.
